The exposure was brief.

more.def: The state of being open to something, such as the sun or cold.
examples: Too much exposure to the sun can burn your skin.
Exposure to cold air made her shiver.
The exposure to loud noise hurt his ears.

easy.def: To show how you feel or what you think.
examples: I express my feelings.
She expressed her thanks.
He expressed his idea in words.

more.def: To let others know what you think or feel, in words, art or actions.
examples: She expressed her thanks with a card.
Painting helps him express his feelings.
The children expressed their ideas in drawings.

easy.def: The look on someone's face.
examples: She had a happy expression.
His expression was sad.
I saw a surprised expression.

more.def: A look on a person's face that shows what they feel.
examples: She had a happy expression on her face.
His expression changed when he heard the news.
The baby's funny expression made us laugh.

easy.def: A group of words with a special meaning.
examples: "Piece of cake" is an expression.
He used a funny expression.
That is a common expression.

more.def: A word or group of words that people use to say something.
examples: "Piece of cake" is an expression that means easy.
She used a funny expression I had never heard.
"It's raining cats and dogs" is a well-known expression.

related.def: Showing no feeling on the face.

easy.def: Showing feelings clearly.
examples: Her face is expressive.
An expressive dancer.
The dog has expressive eyes.

more.def: Showing feelings or thoughts in a clear and lively way.
examples: The dancer's expressive movements told a story.
The actress has an expressive face that shows every feeling.
She gave an expressive reading of the poem.

easy.def: A wide road for fast cars.
examples: We drove on the expressway.
The expressway is wide.
Cars zoom on the expressway.

more.def: A wide road for fast traffic with few stops or crossings.
examples: We drove down the expressway to the city.
The expressway was busy at five o'clock.
Cars sped along the expressway.

easy.def: Very beautiful.
examples: The lace was exquisite.
She wore an exquisite dress.
The cake was exquisite.

more.def: Very beautiful, and made with great care.
examples: The artist painted an exquisite picture of a bird.
The jewelry box had an exquisite design.
She wore an exquisite dress of blue silk.

easy.def: To make longer or reach out.
examples: I extend my hand.
The road extends to the sea.
We extended the visit.

more.def: To stretch out, make longer, or go farther.
examples: The road extends all the way to the sea.
She extended her hand to say hello.
We extended our vacation by two days.

easy.def: An extra part that makes something longer.
examples: The house has an extension.
I plugged in an extension cord.
We got an extension on the homework.

more.def: An extra part added to make something longer, or more time added.
examples: The house has a new extension at the back.
I used an extension cord for the lamp.
The teacher gave us an extension on the project.

easy.def: Very large or covering a lot.
examples: The library has an extensive collection.
An extensive garden.
The damage was extensive.

more.def: Covering a large area or including a lot of things.
examples: The library has an extensive collection of books about animals.
The garden is extensive and has hundreds of different plants.
The storm caused extensive damage to the roofs.

easy.def: How far or how big something is.
examples: We saw the extent of the lake.
The extent of the flood was wide.
I know to some extent.

more.def: The size, length or range of something.
examples: We were amazed at the extent of the cave.
The extent of the damage from the storm was clear by morning.
To some extent, I agree with you.

easy.def: The outside of something.
examples: The exterior of the house is red.
Paint the exterior.
The exterior was clean.

more.def: The outside part or surface of something, such as a building.
examples: The exterior of the old house was painted bright yellow.
The workers repaired the exterior of the school.
The rough exterior of the shell hides a smooth pearl inside.

easy.def: A person whose job is to get rid of bugs and mice.
examples: The exterminator got rid of ants.
We called an exterminator.
An exterminator came to the house.

more.def: A person whose job is to get rid of pests, such as ants, mice or termites, from a building.
examples: The exterminator came to our house to get rid of the ants.
We called an exterminator when we found termites in the wall.
The exterminator told us how to keep mice out.

easy.def: On the outside.
examples: The external wall is red.
An external door.
An external part.

more.def: Located on the outside of something, or coming from outside.
examples: The external walls of the house are painted blue.
My computer has an external speaker that plugs in.
The injury was external, so the doctor only needed to clean it.

easy.def: No longer living anywhere on Earth.
examples: Dinosaurs are extinct.
Some animals may go extinct.
The extinct bird had a big beak.

more.def: No longer existing; having no living members left.
examples: The dodo bird became extinct hundreds of years ago.
Woolly mammoths have been extinct for thousands of years.
People are working to keep tigers from becoming extinct.

easy.def: When a kind of animal or plant dies out for good.
examples: Dinosaurs went into extinction.
The tiger is near extinction.
Extinction is forever.

more.def: The complete dying out of a kind of animal or plant, so that none are left alive.
examples: Dinosaurs went into extinction millions of years ago.
Hunting and loss of homes have pushed many animals toward extinction.
Scientists work to save rare animals from extinction.

easy.def: To put out a fire or a light.
examples: He extinguished the flame.
Extinguish the candle.
Firefighters extinguish fires.

more.def: To put out a fire or a light.
examples: The firefighters extinguished the fire quickly.
He extinguished the candle with a snuffer.
Always extinguish a campfire with water before you leave.

easy.def: A metal can that sprays foam to put out a fire.
examples: Dad grabbed the extinguisher.
A fire extinguisher is red.
The extinguisher was on the wall.

more.def: A container with a spray of foam or gas that is used to put out a small fire.
examples: Dad grabbed the fire extinguisher and put out the grease fire.
Every classroom has a red extinguisher on the wall.
The firefighter showed us how to use an extinguisher.

easy.def: More than usual.
examples: I need an extra pencil.
We have extra time.
Take an extra cookie.

more.def: More than what is usual or needed.
examples: Bring an extra sweater in case it gets cold.
We had extra time before the bus came.
Add an extra spoon of sugar.

easy.def: To pull or take something out.
examples: The dentist will extract a loose tooth.
We extract juice from oranges.
He extracted a coin from the jar.

more.def: To take something out, often with effort or care.
examples: Bees collect nectar and the farmer extracts the honey from the comb.
The scientist extracted a small sample from the rock.
The nurse carefully extracted a splinter from his finger.

easy.def: Something strong made from a plant or food.
examples: I put vanilla extract in the cake.
The extract smells like mint.
Mom bought lemon extract.

more.def: A strong liquid taken from a plant or food, used to give flavor or for medicine.
examples: A few drops of vanilla extract made the cookies smell wonderful.
The soap contains an extract of lavender flowers.
The recipe calls for a teaspoon of almond extract.

easy.def: A short part taken from a book or song.
examples: We read an extract from the book.
The extract was one page.
She read an extract aloud.

more.def: A short piece taken from a longer book, poem or piece of music.
examples: The teacher read us an extract from a famous adventure novel.
The textbook included an extract from a diary written long ago.
We listened to an extract of the symphony before the concert.

easy.def: Done at school but not in a class.
examples: Chess is an extracurricular activity.
I joined an extracurricular club.
Drama is our extracurricular fun.

more.def: Describing activities that students do at school outside of regular lessons, such as clubs and sports.
examples: Her extracurricular activities include band and soccer.
The school offers extracurricular clubs after the last bell.
He is too busy with extracurricular sports to go to the party.

easy.def: Better than ordinary, used after a noun.
examples: A chef extraordinaire.
She is a dancer extraordinaire.
He is a teacher extraordinaire.

more.def: Outstanding, used after a noun to show someone is excellent at something.
examples: He is a chef extraordinaire who cooks wonderful meals.
The chef extraordinaire made a cake with five layers.
Our teacher is a storyteller extraordinaire.

easy.def: Very special and not usual.
examples: The view was extraordinary.
She has an extraordinary gift.
It was an extraordinary day.

more.def: Far beyond what is usual, amazing.
examples: The view from the mountain was extraordinary.
She has an extraordinary talent for music.
It was an extraordinary day I will never forget.

easy.def: A living thing from another planet.
examples: The story had an extraterrestrial.
An extraterrestrial landed.
We saw an extraterrestrial in the movie.

more.def: A living being that comes from a planet other than Earth, such as an alien in stories.
examples: In the movie, a friendly extraterrestrial crash-landed in a backyard.
Scientists search the skies for any sign of an extraterrestrial.
The extraterrestrial in the book had green skin and three eyes.

easy.def: Spending too much.
examples: The party was an extravagance.
Extravagance costs a lot.
A jeweled hat is an extravagance.

more.def: Spending or using more than is needed.
examples: A diamond collar for a dog is an extravagance.
A fancy hat is an extravagance.
The king was known for his extravagance.

easy.def: Spending too much or costing too much.
examples: The party was extravagant.
He bought an extravagant gift.
That is an extravagant hat.

more.def: Costing or using much more than is needed, often in a showy way.
examples: The king held an extravagant feast with hundreds of dishes.
It seemed extravagant to buy ten pairs of shoes.
They gave an extravagant party with fireworks and a live band.

easy.def: A big, fancy show.
examples: The school put on an extravaganza.
The extravaganza was big.
We saw an extravaganza.

more.def: A very large, fancy and exciting show or event.
examples: The school put on a talent extravaganza.
A fireworks extravaganza lit the night sky.
The circus was a colorful extravaganza.

easy.def: Very great.
examples: It was extreme heat.
The cold is extreme.
He took extreme care.

more.def: Much greater than usual, or at the very end of a range.
examples: The extreme heat made us stay inside.
The climbers took extreme care on the icy rocks.
She is an extreme sports fan.
